title: Pokemon Heart & Soul (v2.0.6)
sources: The ROM itself (Heart & Soul 2.0.6, pokeemerald-expansion build): region map section names (each place resolves to a section with maps) and trainer names, teams and levels, read on the PC with throwaway tools
Heart & Soul 2.0 documentation (pokemonhns-development.github.io/pokehns-expansion-documentation): features, gifts and statics, walkthrough, FAQ, encounters
GitHub PokemonHnS-Development/pokehns-expansion (release v2.0.6 notes) and pokemonHnS (1.x README)

pokehns-expansion source at tag Release-v2.0.6 (github.com/PokemonHnS-Development/pokehns-expansion): map scripts (badge flags, trainer placement, Sinjoh/Isles/Teleporter events), map hidden items, species evolutions

milestones.name: Rival: Cherrygrove City
milestones.tips: Elm offers Chikorita, Cyndaquil or Totodile; the rival steals the one strong against yours and battles you at Lv 5 in Cherrygrove after the Mr. Pokémon errand. The ROM keeps three Lv 5 teams named "???", one per starter.
milestones.source: ROM Heart & Soul 2.0.6 trainer table; H&S documentation walkthrough (marked outdated)

milestones.name: Gym 1: Falkner
milestones.badge_note: Zephyr Badge: Flash (field moves need no move slot here: any Pokémon that can learn the HM uses it). TM32.
milestones.tips: Flying types: Pidgey, Noctowl (Lv 8-11). Electric, Ice and Rock moves; Geodude and Mareep from Route 32/46 make it easy.
milestones.source: ROM Heart & Soul 2.0.6 trainer table; H&S documentation walkthrough (marked outdated)

milestones.name: Team Rocket: Proton in Slowpoke Well
milestones.tips: Grunts cut Slowpoke tails; their leader Proton: Koffing, Slowpoke, Houndour (Lv 12-15). Fighting and Psychic moves.
milestones.source: ROM Heart & Soul 2.0.6 trainer table; H&S documentation walkthrough (marked outdated)

milestones.name: Rocket Eto in Slowpoke Well
milestones.tips: A named Rocket on B1F beside Proton: Elekid, Magby, Smoochum (Lv 11). He returns in the Mahogany hideout and under Goldenrod.
milestones.source: ROM Heart & Soul 2.0.6 trainer table; pokehns-expansion Release-v2.0.6 source (SlowpokeWell_B1F script)

milestones.name: Gym 2: Bugsy
milestones.badge_note: Hive Badge: Cut. TM09 Bullet Seed.
milestones.tips: Bug types: Pineco, Ledian, Scyther (Lv 15-16). Fire, Flying and Rock moves; Scyther takes four times from Rock.
milestones.source: ROM Heart & Soul 2.0.6 trainer table; H&S documentation walkthrough (marked outdated)

milestones.name: Rival: Azalea Town
milestones.tips: Zubat, Larvitar and the starter's second stage, Lv 15-18. The rival is stored under the player-named placeholder, so the companion can't look this battle up by name; the level is the ROM's.
milestones.source: ROM Heart & Soul 2.0.6 trainer table; H&S documentation walkthrough (marked outdated)

milestones.name: Gym 3: Whitney
milestones.tips: Normal types: Clefairy, Teddiursa, Miltank (Lv 20-21). Fighting moves; Miltank's Rollout and Milk Drink are the threat: a Fighting type or Machop from the Goldenrod trade.
milestones.source: ROM Heart & Soul 2.0.6 trainer table; H&S documentation walkthrough (marked outdated)

milestones.name: Rival: Burned Tower
milestones.tips: Lv 22-24. The legendary beasts wake here: Entei and Raikou start roaming at Lv 40. The rival is stored under the player-named placeholder, so the companion can't look this battle up by name; the level is the ROM's.
milestones.source: ROM Heart & Soul 2.0.6 trainer table; H&S documentation walkthrough (marked outdated)

milestones.name: Gym 4: Morty
milestones.tips: Ghost types: Haunter, Stantler, Misdreavus, Gengar (Lv 23-25). Dark and Ghost moves; Stantler is Normal (Fighting).
milestones.source: ROM Heart & Soul 2.0.6 trainer table; H&S documentation walkthrough (marked outdated)

milestones.name: Eusine at Cianwood
milestones.tips: Eusine wants Suicune too: Politoed, Hypno, Electrode (Lv 27).
milestones.source: ROM Heart & Soul 2.0.6 trainer table; H&S documentation walkthrough (marked outdated)

milestones.name: Gym 5: Chuck
milestones.badge_note: Storm Badge: Fly. TM01 Focus Punch.
milestones.tips: Fighting types: Hitmontop, Primeape, Sudowoodo, Poliwrath (Lv 29-31). Psychic and Flying moves. Gyms 5-7 scale with your badges: the ROM has Chuck at 31, 36 and 38.
milestones.source: ROM Heart & Soul 2.0.6 trainer table; H&S documentation walkthrough (marked outdated)

milestones.name: Gym 6: Jasmine
milestones.tips: Steel types: Skarmory, Corsola, Magneton, Scizor, Steelix (Lv 35-36). Fire, Fighting and Ground moves; Scizor takes four times from Fire. Cure Amphy in the lighthouse first (Cianwood's medicine).
milestones.source: ROM Heart & Soul 2.0.6 trainer table; H&S documentation walkthrough (marked outdated)

milestones.name: Rocket hideout in Mahogany
milestones.tips: After the red Gyarados at the Lake of Rage, Lance joins you: Petrel (Pineco, Larvitar, Magcargo, Cloyster (Lv 30)), then a double battle beside Lance against Ariana (Arbok, Persian, Vileplume (Lv 30-31)).
milestones.source: ROM Heart & Soul 2.0.6 trainer table; H&S documentation walkthrough (marked outdated)

milestones.name: Rocket Eto in the Mahogany hideout
milestones.tips: Jynx, Poliwhirl, Magmar, Electabuzz (Lv 28) on B3F; he guards one of the passwords to the boss room.
milestones.source: ROM Heart & Soul 2.0.6 trainer table; pokehns-expansion Release-v2.0.6 source (RocketHideout_B3F script); H&S documentation walkthrough (marked outdated)

milestones.name: Gym 7: Pryce
milestones.badge_note: Glacier Badge. TM07. The Radio Tower takeover starts once you hold seven badges.
milestones.tips: Ice types: Cloyster, Sneasel, Jynx, Dewgong, Mamoswine (Lv 37-38). Fire, Fighting, Rock and Steel moves; Piloswine/Mamoswine fear Water and Grass too.
milestones.source: ROM Heart & Soul 2.0.6 trainer table; H&S documentation walkthrough (marked outdated)

milestones.name: Rival: Goldenrod Underground
milestones.tips: Pupitar, Golbat, the starter's final stage and two more (Lv 38-40), in the switch room under the Department Store. The rival is stored under the player-named placeholder, so the companion can't look this battle up by name; the level is the ROM's.
milestones.source: ROM Heart & Soul 2.0.6 trainer table; pokehns-expansion Release-v2.0.6 source (GoldenrodCity_UndergroundSwitches script)

milestones.name: Rocket Eto in the underground storage
milestones.tips: Poliwrath, Magmar, Jynx, Electabuzz, Rhydon (Lv 36) in the storage room where the real director is held; the director then hands over the Card Key for the Radio Tower.
milestones.source: ROM Heart & Soul 2.0.6 trainer table; pokehns-expansion Release-v2.0.6 source (GoldenrodCity_UndergroundStorage script)

milestones.name: Team Rocket takes the Radio Tower
milestones.tips: Petrel disguised as the director (Forretress, Pupitar, Magcargo, Cloyster (Lv 38-39)), Proton (Muk, Nidoqueen, Weezing, Nidoking, Rhydon (Lv 36-38)), Ariana (Arbok, Persian, Vileplume, Gyarados, Murkrow (Lv 39-40)) and Archer on the top floor (Porygon-Z, Tauros, Gyarados, Houndoom, Slowbro (Lv 38-40)); the rival waits in the Goldenrod underground (Lv 38-40).
milestones.source: ROM Heart & Soul 2.0.6 trainer table; H&S documentation walkthrough (marked outdated)

milestones.name: Gym 8: Clair
milestones.tips: Dragons and Water: Dragonair, Gyarados, Lapras, Dudunsparce, Kingdra (Lv 42-45). Ice, Dragon and Fairy moves; Kingdra is only weak to Dragon and Fairy. Finish the Dragon's Den test for the badge and TM02.
milestones.source: ROM Heart & Soul 2.0.6 trainer table; H&S documentation walkthrough (marked outdated)

milestones.name: Rival: Victory Road
milestones.tips: Six Pokémon now, a Tyranitar on top at Lv 48. The rival is stored under the player-named placeholder, so the companion can't look this battle up by name; the level is the ROM's.
milestones.source: ROM Heart & Soul 2.0.6 trainer table; H&S documentation walkthrough (marked outdated)

milestones.name: Elite Four: Will
milestones.tips: Girafarig, Slowking, Espeon, Slowbro, Xatu (Lv 48-50). Dark, Ghost and Bug moves.
milestones.source: ROM Heart & Soul 2.0.6 trainer table; H&S documentation walkthrough (marked outdated)

milestones.name: Elite Four: Koga
milestones.tips: Ariados, Qwilfish, Muk, Venomoth, Crobat (Lv 50-52). Psychic and Ground moves.
milestones.source: ROM Heart & Soul 2.0.6 trainer table; H&S documentation walkthrough (marked outdated)

milestones.name: Elite Four: Bruno
milestones.tips: Hitmonchan, Heracross, Hitmonlee, Steelix, Machamp (Lv 52-54). Psychic, Flying and Fairy moves; Steelix wants Fire or Water.
milestones.source: ROM Heart & Soul 2.0.6 trainer table; H&S documentation walkthrough (marked outdated)

milestones.name: Elite Four: Karen
milestones.tips: Umbreon, Gengar, Vileplume, Honchkrow, Houndoom (Lv 53-55). Fighting, Bug and Fairy moves.
milestones.source: ROM Heart & Soul 2.0.6 trainer table; H&S documentation walkthrough (marked outdated)

milestones.name: Champion Lance
milestones.tips: Gyarados, Dragonite, Charizard, Dragonite, Aerodactyl, Dragonite (Lv 54-56). Ice moves (Dragonite takes four times), Rock or Electric for Charizard, Gyarados and Aerodactyl.
milestones.source: ROM Heart & Soul 2.0.6 trainer table; H&S documentation walkthrough (marked outdated)

milestones.name: To Kanto on the S.S. Aqua
milestones.tips: After the league, Elm's ticket gets you on the S.S. Aqua from Olivine to Vermilion. Kanto's wild Pokémon are in the 40s; the leaders can be fought in almost any order.
milestones.source: H&S documentation walkthrough (marked outdated)

milestones.name: Kanto gym: Lt. Surge
milestones.tips: Electrode, Magnezone, Lanturn, Manectric, Electivire, Raichu (Lv 57-60). Ground moves.
milestones.source: ROM Heart & Soul 2.0.6 trainer table; badge flag from the gym script (pokehns-expansion Release-v2.0.6 source)

milestones.name: Kanto gym: Erika
milestones.tips: Jumpluff, Roserade, Tangrowth, Venusaur, Victreebel, Bellossom (Lv 60-62). Fire, Flying, Ice and Poison moves.
milestones.source: ROM Heart & Soul 2.0.6 trainer table; badge flag from the gym script (pokehns-expansion Release-v2.0.6 source)

milestones.name: Kanto gym: Misty
milestones.tips: Golduck, Quagsire, Vaporeon, Milotic, Lapras, Starmie (Lv 61-63). Electric and Grass moves.
milestones.source: ROM Heart & Soul 2.0.6 trainer table; badge flag from the gym script (pokehns-expansion Release-v2.0.6 source)

milestones.name: Kanto gym: Janine
milestones.tips: Weezing, Muk, Swalot, Nidoqueen, Crobat, Venomoth (Lv 61-64). Psychic and Ground moves.
milestones.source: ROM Heart & Soul 2.0.6 trainer table; badge flag from the gym script (pokehns-expansion Release-v2.0.6 source)

milestones.name: Kanto gym: Sabrina
milestones.tips: Mr. Mime, Jynx, Slowbro, Wobbuffet, Espeon, Alakazam (Lv 64-66). Dark, Ghost and Bug moves.
milestones.source: ROM Heart & Soul 2.0.6 trainer table; badge flag from the gym script (pokehns-expansion Release-v2.0.6 source)

milestones.name: Kanto gym: Brock
milestones.tips: Golem, Aerodactyl, Kabutops, Omastar, Relicanth, Kleavor (Lv 66). Water and Grass moves (Fighting and Ground for most).
milestones.source: ROM Heart & Soul 2.0.6 trainer table; badge flag from the gym script (pokehns-expansion Release-v2.0.6 source)

milestones.name: Rival: Mt. Moon
milestones.tips: All six at Lv 64. The rival is stored under the player-named placeholder, so the companion can't look this battle up by name; the level is the ROM's.
milestones.source: ROM Heart & Soul 2.0.6 trainer table; H&S documentation walkthrough (marked outdated)

milestones.name: Kanto gym: Blaine
milestones.tips: Rapidash, Magmortar, Houndoom, Magcargo, Torkoal, Camerupt (Lv 65-67). Water, Ground and Rock moves. As in HGSS his gym is inside the Seafoam Islands, reached from Cinnabar.
milestones.source: ROM Heart & Soul 2.0.6 trainer table; badge flag from the gym script (pokehns-expansion Release-v2.0.6 source)

milestones.name: Kanto gym: Blue
milestones.tips: Rhyperior, Pidgeot, Machamp, Exeggutor, Tyranitar, Arcanine (Lv 67-69). A mixed team: bring broad coverage. He opens his gym once you hold 15 badges and have talked to him on Cinnabar.
milestones.source: ROM Heart & Soul 2.0.6 trainer table; badge flag from the gym script (pokehns-expansion Release-v2.0.6 source)

milestones.name: Rival: Indigo Plateau
milestones.tips: The last rival fight waits in the Indigo Plateau Pokémon Center: six at Lv 68 with Tyranitar, Ursaluna and Crobat. The rival is stored under the player-named placeholder, so the companion can't look this battle up by name; the level is the ROM's.
milestones.source: ROM Heart & Soul 2.0.6 trainer table; pokehns-expansion Release-v2.0.6 source (IndigoPlateau_PokemonCenter script)

milestones.name: Kanto League: Will
milestones.tips: The second League run: Gardevoir, Jynx, Exeggutor, Grumpig, Slowbro, Xatu (Lv 66-68). Dark, Ghost and Bug moves.
milestones.source: ROM Heart & Soul 2.0.6 trainer table; pokehns-expansion Release-v2.0.6 source (Will's room script)

milestones.name: Kanto League: Koga
milestones.tips: Tentacruel, Muk, Swalot, Nidoking, Venomoth, Crobat (Lv 67-68). Ground and Psychic moves.
milestones.source: ROM Heart & Soul 2.0.6 trainer table

milestones.name: Kanto League: Bruno
milestones.tips: Steelix, Poliwrath, Heracross, Hariyama, Hitmontop, Machamp (Lv 67-68). Flying, Psychic and Fairy; Fire for Steelix and Heracross.
milestones.source: ROM Heart & Soul 2.0.6 trainer table

milestones.name: Kanto League: Karen
milestones.tips: Umbreon, Weavile, Persian, Honchkrow, Absol, Houndoom (Lv 67-69). Fighting, Bug and Fairy moves.
milestones.source: ROM Heart & Soul 2.0.6 trainer table

milestones.name: Kanto League: Champion Lance
milestones.tips: Salamence, Dragonite, Gyarados, Charizard, Aerodactyl, Altaria (Lv 68-70). Ice and Fairy moves; Rock for Charizard, Aerodactyl and Gyarados's Flying side. Winning this run makes you Kanto Champion (the Hall of Fame sets it), which the Dojo and Red rematch tiers check.
milestones.source: ROM Heart & Soul 2.0.6 trainer table; pokehns-expansion Release-v2.0.6 source (Champion's room and Hall of Fame scripts)

milestones.name: Giovanni (Celebi event)
milestones.tips: With Celebi first in your party, enter the radio room at Tohjo Falls: Kangaskhan, Honchkrow, Nidoqueen, Persian, Ursaluna, Nidoking (Lv 60-62). With Celebi first on Route 22 you see a Giovanni and rival scene instead.
milestones.source: ROM Heart & Soul 2.0.6 trainer table; Heart & Soul 2.0 documentation (pokemonhns-development.github.io)

milestones.name: The Kimono Girls
milestones.tips: Five back-to-back battles with one Eeveelution each at Lv 48; part of what Ho-Oh or Lugia asks for.
milestones.source: ROM Heart & Soul 2.0.6 trainer table; Heart & Soul 2.0 documentation (pokemonhns-development.github.io)

milestones.name: Red on Mt. Silver
milestones.tips: With 16 badges, talk to Oak; Red waits at the summit: Pikachu, Snorlax, Charizard, Venusaur, Blastoise, Espeon (Lv 77-93). A later Red team tops at 95.
milestones.source: ROM Heart & Soul 2.0.6 trainer table; H&S documentation walkthrough (marked outdated)

milestones.name: Steven in the Sinjoh Ruins
milestones.tips: The bonus Sinjoh story: Skarmory, Omastar, Claydol, Aggron, Kleavor, Metagross (Lv 77-79). Fire and Ground moves cover most of it; Ground and Fighting for Metagross and Aggron.
milestones.source: ROM Heart & Soul 2.0.6 trainer table; pokehns-expansion Release-v2.0.6 source (SinjohRuins script)

milestones.name: Kimono sisters in New Sinjoh
milestones.tips: Three more Kimono Girls, one Eeveelution each at Lv 70: Leafeon, Glaceon, Sylveon. Fire for Leafeon and Glaceon, Steel or Poison for Sylveon.
milestones.source: ROM Heart & Soul 2.0.6 trainer table; pokehns-expansion Release-v2.0.6 source (NewSinjoh_KimonoHideout script)

milestones.name: Sage Finley on Route 50
milestones.tips: Flygon, Salamence, Kingdra, Alolan Exeggutor (Lv 70): a dragon team, so Ice and Fairy moves.
milestones.source: ROM Heart & Soul 2.0.6 trainer table; pokehns-expansion Release-v2.0.6 source (Route50 script)

milestones.name: The Milkman in New Sinjoh
milestones.tips: Six Miltank, the last at Lv 80. Fighting moves; mind Miltank's healing.
milestones.source: ROM Heart & Soul 2.0.6 trainer table; pokehns-expansion Release-v2.0.6 source (NewSinjoh script)

milestones.name: Samson Oak on Melemele Isle
milestones.tips: On the Alola Isles: Alolan Raichu, Exeggutor, Ninetales, Golem and Muk with Tropius (Lv 70). Ground moves hit Raichu, Golem and Muk; Steel and Fire for Ninetales.
milestones.source: ROM Heart & Soul 2.0.6 trainer table; pokehns-expansion Release-v2.0.6 source (Melemele_PlayerHouse script)

milestones.name: League and Red after the Sinjoh story
milestones.tips: Once you are Kanto Champion and the Sinjoh story is over, the Elite Four and Lance bring Lv 74-79 teams with regional forms, and Red on Mt. Silver tops out at Lv 95 (Pikachu).
milestones.source: ROM Heart & Soul 2.0.6 trainer table; pokehns-expansion Release-v2.0.6 source (League and Mt. Silver summit scripts)

milestones.name: Leader rematches after the Sinjoh story
milestones.tips: The Saffron Dojo's last tier: all sixteen leaders with Lv 69-73 teams, many with regional forms (Weezing-G, Raichu-A, Marowak-A).
milestones.source: ROM Heart & Soul 2.0.6 trainer table; pokehns-expansion Release-v2.0.6 source (SaffronCity_FightingDojoVIP script)

milestones.name: Leader rematches
milestones.tips: At the Saffron Dojo every leader you have met can be rematched for 10 BP: the Johto leaders with Lv 63-68 teams, the Kanto leaders with their gym teams. Once you are Kanto Champion and the Sinjoh story is finished they bring Lv 69-73 teams.
milestones.source: ROM Heart & Soul 2.0.6 trainer table; pokehns-expansion Release-v2.0.6 source (Saffron Dojo script)

milestones.name: Ho-Oh (Tin Tower)
milestones.tips: On the roof by day with the Rainbow Wing, after 8 badges, Elm's Master Ball and the Kimono Girls (the statics page says after Dragon's Den or Pewter: unclear). Baoba's question on Route 39 decides: the bird you pick is Lv 50, the other Lv 70.
milestones.source: Heart & Soul 2.0 documentation (pokemonhns-development.github.io)

milestones.name: Lugia (Whirl Islands)
milestones.tips: In the Whirl Islands chamber with the Silver Wing, under the same rules as Ho-Oh.
milestones.source: Heart & Soul 2.0 documentation (pokemonhns-development.github.io)

milestones.name: Suicune (Route 25)
milestones.tips: Chased through Cianwood, Route 42, Vermilion and Route 14; it waits on Route 25 after you beat Misty.
milestones.source: Heart & Soul 2.0 documentation (pokemonhns-development.github.io)

milestones.name: Celebi (Ilex Forest)
milestones.tips: Kurt checks the GS Ball; take it to the Ilex shrine. The GS Ball comes back after the Kanto Elite Four.
milestones.source: Heart & Soul 2.0 documentation (pokemonhns-development.github.io)

milestones.name: Mewtwo (Cerulean Cave)
milestones.tips: With 16 badges, in Cerulean Cave.
milestones.source: Heart & Soul 2.0 documentation (pokemonhns-development.github.io)

milestones.name: Kyogre, Groudon, Rayquaza
milestones.tips: With 16 badges: Kyogre in a cave off Route 19, Groudon in a secret Seafoam cave, Rayquaza in the Embedded Tower, all Lv 70.
milestones.source: Heart & Soul 2.0 documentation (pokemonhns-development.github.io)

milestones.name: Arceus and the Regis (Sinjoh Ruins)
milestones.tips: Arceus at Lv 80 in the Sinjoh Ruins, with Regirock, Regice, Registeel, Regigigas, Regieleki and Regidrago at Lv 80.
milestones.source: Heart & Soul 2.0 documentation (pokemonhns-development.github.io)

milestones.name: Zapdos (Route 10)
milestones.tips: Lv 50 outside the Power Plant once the Machine Part is back; run and re-enter to meet it again.
milestones.source: H&S 2.0 documentation: Gifts & Statics; H&S documentation walkthrough (marked outdated)

milestones.name: Articuno (Seafoam Islands)
milestones.tips: Lv 50 on B1F after a bike and ice puzzle; resets if you run.
milestones.source: H&S 2.0 documentation: Gifts & Statics; H&S documentation walkthrough (marked outdated)

milestones.name: Moltres (Mt. Silver)
milestones.tips: Lv 50 in its own room on Mt. Silver 1F; resets if you run.
milestones.source: H&S 2.0 documentation: Gifts & Statics

milestones.name: Jirachi (Mt. Moon)
milestones.tips: Lv 50 at Mt. Moon Square at night, by touching the white rock; waiting for the next night brings it back.
milestones.source: H&S 2.0 documentation: Gifts & Statics; H&S documentation walkthrough (marked outdated)

milestones.name: Latias and Latios
milestones.tips: Steven's Eon Ticket from the Kanto Safari Zone opens Southern Island: one Lati waits there at Lv 50, the other roams Kanto at Lv 60.
milestones.source: H&S 2.0 documentation: Gifts & Statics; H&S documentation walkthrough (marked outdated)

milestones.name: Mew (Faraway Island)
milestones.tips: Lv 50; you can't run and it doesn't come back, so save first.
milestones.source: H&S 2.0 documentation: Gifts & Statics; H&S documentation walkthrough (marked outdated); H&S 2.0 documentation: FAQ

milestones.name: Deoxys (Birth Island)
milestones.tips: The Auroraticket from south Olivine opens Birth Island: solve the timed triangle puzzle for Deoxys at Lv 70. It doesn't come back, so save first.
milestones.source: H&S 2.0 documentation: Gifts & Statics; H&S documentation walkthrough (marked outdated); H&S 2.0 documentation: FAQ

milestones.name: The Tapus (Alola Isles)
milestones.tips: Tapu Koko on Melemele, Tapu Lele on Akala, Tapu Bulu in the Ula'ula forest and Tapu Fini on Poni, all Lv 60.
milestones.source: H&S 2.0 documentation: Gifts & Statics

steps.title: Challenge settings at the start
steps.text: The new-game settings cover the randomizer, Nuzlocke, EXP rate, level caps, shiny odds, IVs, EVs, party size and mono-type; the split and Fairy are toggles too. Some can be eased later at a Pokémon Center, never made harder.

steps.title: HMs need no slots
steps.text: Any Pokémon that can learn an HM can use it in the field once you have the badge.

steps.title: Bill's Eevee
steps.text: Meet Bill in Ecruteak, then he gives a Lv 20 Eevee in Goldenrod.

steps.title: Dragon's Den quiz
steps.text: The Dragon's Den shrine gives a Lv 15 Dratini; answer all the elder's questions right for a shiny one.

steps.title: Restore the Power Plant
steps.text: The Machine Part turns up in Cerulean's gym; returning it gives TM25, and Zapdos (Lv 50) appears on Route 10.

steps.title: Mr. Pokémon's egg
steps.text: On Route 30 Mr. Pokémon hands you the Mystery Egg and Oak the Pokédex; back at the lab Elm takes the egg (it hatches later at the Violet Pokémon Center) and gives you Poké Balls.

steps.title: Sprout Tower
steps.text: Climb Sprout Tower and beat Elder Li's sages for HM05 Flash before the Violet gym.

steps.title: Ruins of Alph
steps.text: Solve the Kabuto puzzle and the lab revives the fossil. The back rooms want a matching Pokémon first in your party.
steps.source: H&S documentation walkthrough (marked outdated); H&S 2.0 documentation: FAQ

steps.title: Kurt's Berry Balls
steps.text: After the Slowpoke Well, Kurt turns berries into special Poké Balls (no Apricorns in this game).
steps.source: H&S documentation walkthrough (marked outdated); H&S 2.0 documentation: Features

steps.title: Cut in Ilex Forest
steps.text: Herd the charcoal maker's Farfetch'd back through Ilex Forest (approach it from behind) for HM01 Cut.

steps.title: Goldenrod errands
steps.text: The bike shop gives a Bicycle, the Radio Tower a radio card, and the underground the Coin Case; the Day Care is on Route 34.

steps.title: The odd tree on Route 36
steps.text: After Whitney, the Flower Shop gives the Squirtbottle: water the tree on Route 36 to fight Sudowoodo (Lv 20), then get HM06 Rock Smash nearby. The shop also sells Nature Mints.
steps.source: H&S documentation walkthrough (marked outdated); H&S 2.0 documentation: Gifts & Statics; H&S 2.0 documentation: FAQ

steps.title: HM03 Surf
steps.text: The Ecruteak Dance Theater gives HM03 Surf; Morty's badge lets you use it.

steps.title: Baoba's question
steps.text: On Route 39 Baoba asks what colour the shadow was: your answer decides which of Ho-Oh and Lugia you meet first at Lv 50 (the other is Lv 70).
steps.source: H&S documentation walkthrough (marked outdated); H&S 2.0 documentation: Gifts & Statics

steps.title: Medicine for Amphy
steps.text: Jasmine waits with the sick Ampharos at the top of the lighthouse: the Cianwood pharmacy's SecretPotion cures it, and then she opens her gym.

steps.title: HM02 Fly
steps.text: Chuck's wife gives HM02 Fly after his badge.

steps.title: The red Gyarados
steps.text: At the Lake of Rage the shiny Gyarados (Lv 30) leaves a Red Scale; Lance then asks you to the Mahogany shop.
steps.source: H&S documentation walkthrough (marked outdated); H&S 2.0 documentation: Gifts & Statics

steps.title: HM08 Whirlpool
steps.text: Beat or catch the three Electrode (Lv 30) powering the hideout's signal: Lance gives HM08 Whirlpool.
steps.source: H&S documentation walkthrough (marked outdated); H&S 2.0 documentation: Gifts & Statics

steps.title: Radio Tower keys
steps.text: The fake director on the tower gives the Basement Key; the real one, held under the Department Store, gives the Card Key for the upper floors.

steps.title: Ice Path
steps.text: HM07 Waterfall lies in the Ice Path on the way to Blackthorn.

steps.title: Elm's Master Ball
steps.text: After the eighth badge Elm gives a Master Ball and sends you to the Kimono Girls: beating them is the last thing Ho-Oh and Lugia need.
steps.source: H&S documentation walkthrough (marked outdated); H&S 2.0 documentation: FAQ

steps.title: S.S. Aqua errand
steps.text: Oak upgrades the Pokédex at the Olivine port. On board find the old man's granddaughter for a Metal Coat.

steps.title: Steven at Silph Co.
steps.text: Steven gives a Hoenn starter at Lv 5 (by the stone you pick) and an Up-Grade.
steps.source: H&S documentation walkthrough (marked outdated); H&S 2.0 documentation: Gifts & Statics

steps.title: Wake Snorlax
steps.text: The Lavender Radio Tower's radio upgrade wakes the Vermilion Snorlax (Lv 50) that blocks Diglett's Cave, the way to Pewter.
steps.source: H&S documentation walkthrough (marked outdated); H&S 2.0 documentation: Gifts & Statics

steps.title: Kanto Safari Zone
steps.text: Steven runs the Fuchsia Safari Zone. Baoba asks you to catch Hoenn Pokémon there for him; his rewards pay for the Brush, Mountain and Cave areas.

steps.title: Bill's grandpa
steps.text: In the Route 25 house, show Bill's grandpa the Pokémon he describes for items. Showing a Slowpoke earns the Galarica Cuff and Wreath and unlocks Bill's Teleporter.
steps.source: H&S documentation walkthrough (marked outdated); pokehns-expansion Release-v2.0.6 source (Route25_BillsHouse script)

steps.title: The Azure Flute
steps.text: On Mt. Silver 2F you find the Azure Flute. Show it to the researcher in the Mt. Silver Pokémon Center to start the optional Sinjoh content (Snowswept Cavern, Routes 49-50, New Sinjoh, the ruins).
steps.source: pokehns-expansion Release-v2.0.6 source (MtSilver_2F and MtSilver_PokemonCenter scripts)

steps.title: Plates in Sinjoh
steps.text: All 17 plates are in the Sinjoh area: noble Pokémon drop them (Machamp in Snowswept Cavern: Fist Plate), and Skier Skylar on Route 49 battles you for the Sky Plate.
steps.source: H&S 2.0 documentation: FAQ; pokehns-expansion Release-v2.0.6 source (SnowsweptCavern and Route49 scripts)

steps.title: To the Alola Isles
steps.text: Buy a Strange Souvenir at the Mt. Moon gift shop: the captain on Route 13 then takes you to the Alola Isles, with Alolan forms and the Tapus.
steps.source: pokehns-expansion Release-v2.0.6 source (MtMoon_Shop and Route13 scripts); H&S 2.0 documentation: Gifts & Statics

secrets.text: A house in Cianwood lends a Lv 20 Shuckle.
A Lv 25 Tyrogue in Mt. Mortar.
A Lv 25 Tentacool at the Cianwood Pokémon Center, only if no party member can Surf.
The Ruins of Alph revive fossils at Lv 20 (Kabuto at Lv 5).
Silph Co. gives the Hoenn starters at Lv 5.
Paldean Wooper in New Sinjoh.
A Lv 20 Lapras on Union Cave B2F, at night only.
The shiny red Gyarados at Lv 30 at the Lake of Rage.
A Lv 50 Snorlax at Vermilion, woken with the radio upgrade.
The spiky-eared Pichu at Lv 35 in Viridian Forest.
Articuno on Seafoam B1F, Zapdos on Route 10, Moltres in a Mt. Silver room, all Lv 50.
Jirachi at Lv 50 outside Mt. Moon (re-rolls at night).
With Steven's Eon Ticket (from the Safari Zone), one Lati at Lv 50 on Southern Island; the other roams Kanto at Lv 60.
Mew at Lv 50 on Faraway Island; Deoxys at Lv 70 on Birth Island with the Auroraticket from Olivine.
Violet: a Bellsprout for an Onix.
Goldenrod: a Drowzee for a Machop (Dept. Store 6F).
Jasmine trades her Steelix 'Rusty' for any Pokémon.
Blackthorn: a Dodrio for a Mr. Mime.
Pewter: Xatu for Haunter and Rhyhorn for Bonsly.
The Game Corner has Abra, Clefairy, Dratini, Munchlax and Porygon.
Celadon Mansion awards a diploma for a complete Pokédex.
Each Kanto route has a 5% Hoenn Pokémon in place of swarms; the Hoenn Sound radio raises it.
Two hidden Nuggets in Cherrygrove City. The Itemfinder helps.
Hidden on Route 32: a Shell Bell, a Heart Scale and a Great Ball. The Itemfinder helps.
Hidden outside the Ruins of Alph: a Rare Candy and a Nugget. The Itemfinder helps.
Hidden in Dark Cave: a Black Flute and a Max Ether (south side), a Big Mushroom and a Revive (north side). The Itemfinder helps.
A hidden Rare Candy on Route 34. The Itemfinder helps.
A hidden Heart Scale in Cianwood City. The Itemfinder helps.
Hidden at the Lake of Rage: Choice Specs, a Rare Candy, a Max Revive and a Max Potion. The Itemfinder helps.
A hidden Dubious Disc on Route 42 (Porygon2 into Porygon-Z). The Itemfinder helps.
Hidden in Mt. Mortar: an Iron Ball and a Nugget (1F), an HP Up and a Full Incense (2F). The Itemfinder helps.
Hidden on Route 47: the Lucky Egg, a Wave Incense, a Lagging Tail and a Pearl. The Itemfinder helps.
Hidden in Vermilion City: a Big Pearl, a Pearl String and a Heart Scale. The Itemfinder helps.
Hidden in Rock Tunnel: an Oval Stone (B1F) and an Iron (1F). The Itemfinder helps.
A hidden Light Clay on Route 9. The Itemfinder helps.
Hidden on Route 10: the Rock Polish TM and an Ultra Ball. The Itemfinder helps.
Hidden on Route 8: the Torment TM. The Itemfinder helps.
A hidden Lucky Punch on Route 14. The Itemfinder helps.
Hidden side by side on Route 20: the Deep Sea Tooth and the Deep Sea Scale (Clamperl). The Itemfinder helps.
Hidden in the Seafoam Islands: a Water Stone, a Grip Claw and a Max Revive (B1F), a Rare Candy (1F). The Itemfinder helps.
Hidden in Viridian Forest: a Leaf Stone, a Blue Flute and two Big Mushrooms. The Itemfinder helps.
Wise Glasses hidden in Pewter City. The Itemfinder helps.
Hidden in Cerulean Cave: an Electirizer, a Dusk Stone and a Black Sludge (B2F). The Itemfinder helps.
Hidden on Mt. Silver: an Expert Belt (waterfall room), a Dawn Stone, a Reaper Cloth and a Full Restore. The Itemfinder helps.
The Soul Dew is hidden inside Southern Island. The Itemfinder helps.
Hidden on Route 49: a King's Rock, an Ice Stone and an Ultra Ball. The Itemfinder helps.
A hidden Never-Melt Ice in Snowswept Cavern. The Itemfinder helps.
Rudy in the Route 35 gate lends a Lv 20 Spearow, "Kenya", holding Retro Mail.
Sudowoodo (Lv 20) on Route 36, woken with the Squirtbottle; resets if you run.
Three Electrode (Lv 30) on the hideout's B2F; run and re-enter to try again.
Olivine: a Krabby for a Voltorb, "Billy".
Power Plant entrance: a Dugtrio for a Magneton, "Maggie", holding a Metal Coat.
Safari Zone entrance: Steven trades a Beldum, "Iron", holding a Metal Coat, for a Forretress.
Battle Frontier lounge: a Skitty for a Meowth.
Jessica on Melemele trades a Paldean Tauros once: the breed depends on your starter (Aqua for Cyndaquil, Blaze for Totodile, Combat for Chikorita).
Static Alolan forms at Lv 60 on the Isles: Raichu (Akala Forest), Exeggutor (Poni Isle), Golem (Poni Cave), Dugtrio and Marowak (Akala Cave), Ninetales, Sandslash and Muk (Ula'ula caves).

Bill's Teleporter in the Route 25 house turns some Pokémon (Meowth, Ponyta, Slowpoke line, Farfetch'd, Weezing, Mr. Mime, the three birds, Corsola, Zigzagoon, Linoone) into their Galarian forms, permanently.
The Amulet Coin is in the Goldenrod Department Store basement; it works if anyone in the party holds it.
The Odd Egg hatches shiny 14% of the time; the Day Care bookshelves list what it can hatch.
Larvitar can be caught before Falkner: Dark Cave south side by day, 5%, Lv 2-4.
In the Ice Path a Delibird gives TM14 Blizzard for an Aspear Berry.
A berry tree on Route 43 gives Leppa Berries.
Route 47's grass has Chansey: good EXP before the League.
secrets.source: H&S 2.0 documentation: FAQ; H&S documentation walkthrough (marked outdated)

secrets.text: IVs can't be changed; EV-lowering berries grow in Kanto.
Ability Capsules come from the Saffron Dojo and the Battle Frontier.

evolutions.name: Kadabra
evolutions.text: No trade needed: Kadabra evolves at Lv 42 (Machoke and Graveler at 38, Haunter at 42); a trade still works.

evolutions.name: Onix
evolutions.text: Use a Metal Coat on it (like a stone) for Steelix, or trade it holding one.
evolutions.source: pokehns-expansion Release-v2.0.6 source (species_info evolutions); H&S documentation walkthrough (marked outdated)

evolutions.name: Seadra
evolutions.text: Use a Dragon Scale on it for Kingdra, or trade it holding one.
evolutions.source: pokehns-expansion Release-v2.0.6 source (species_info evolutions); H&S documentation walkthrough (marked outdated)

evolutions.name: Slowpoke
evolutions.text: Slowbro at Lv 37; use a King's Rock on it for Slowking. Galarian Slowpoke (Bill's Teleporter) takes the Galarica Cuff (Slowbro) or Wreath (Slowking) from Bill's grandpa.
evolutions.source: pokehns-expansion Release-v2.0.6 source (species_info evolutions); H&S documentation walkthrough (marked outdated)

evolutions.name: Porygon
evolutions.text: Use the Up-Grade on Porygon (Silph Co. gift) for Porygon2, then the Dubious Disc (hidden on Route 42) for Porygon-Z; trading with them held works too.
evolutions.source: pokehns-expansion Release-v2.0.6 source (species_info evolutions); H&S documentation walkthrough (marked outdated)

evolutions.name: Machoke
evolutions.text: Machamp at Lv 38, no trade needed.

evolutions.name: Graveler
evolutions.text: Golem at Lv 38, no trade needed (Alolan Graveler likewise).

evolutions.name: Haunter
evolutions.text: Gengar at Lv 42, no trade needed.

evolutions.name: Poliwhirl
evolutions.text: Water Stone for Poliwrath; use a King's Rock for Politoed.

evolutions.name: Scyther
evolutions.text: Use a Metal Coat for Scizor; a Black Augurite for Kleavor.

evolutions.name: Rhydon
evolutions.text: Use a Protector for Rhyperior.

evolutions.name: Electabuzz
evolutions.text: Use an Electirizer for Electivire (one is hidden in Cerulean Cave).
evolutions.source: pokehns-expansion Release-v2.0.6 source (species_info evolutions); pokehns-expansion Release-v2.0.6 source (map hidden items)

evolutions.name: Magmar
evolutions.text: Use a Magmarizer for Magmortar.

evolutions.name: Porygon2
evolutions.text: Use the Dubious Disc for Porygon-Z.

evolutions.name: Dusclops
evolutions.text: Use a Reaper Cloth for Dusknoir (one is hidden on Mt. Silver).
evolutions.source: pokehns-expansion Release-v2.0.6 source (species_info evolutions); pokehns-expansion Release-v2.0.6 source (map hidden items)

evolutions.name: Clamperl
evolutions.text: Use the Deep Sea Tooth for Huntail or the Deep Sea Scale for Gorebyss: both are hidden on Route 20.
evolutions.source: pokehns-expansion Release-v2.0.6 source (species_info evolutions); pokehns-expansion Release-v2.0.6 source (map hidden items)

evolutions.name: Feebas
evolutions.text: Level up with high Beauty, or use a Prism Scale, for Milotic.

evolutions.name: Magneton
evolutions.text: Level up on Route 10 or in the Power Plant, or use a Thunder Stone, for Magnezone.

evolutions.name: Nosepass
evolutions.text: Level up on Route 10 or in the Power Plant, or use a Thunder Stone, for Probopass.

evolutions.name: Eevee
evolutions.text: Stones: Thunder, Water, Fire, Shiny (Sylveon), Leaf (Leafeon), Ice (Glaceon). Or level up in Ilex/Viridian Forest for Leafeon, in the Ice Path/Seafoam for Glaceon; high friendship by day for Espeon, at night for Umbreon.

evolutions.name: Lickitung
evolutions.text: Level up knowing Rollout for Lickilicky (a Pewter NPC teaches Rollout).
evolutions.source: pokehns-expansion Release-v2.0.6 source (species_info evolutions); H&S documentation walkthrough (marked outdated)

evolutions.name: Tangela
evolutions.text: Level up knowing Ancient Power for Tangrowth.

evolutions.name: Aipom
evolutions.text: Level up knowing Double Hit for Ambipom.

evolutions.name: Yanma
evolutions.text: Level up knowing Ancient Power for Yanmega.

evolutions.name: Piloswine
evolutions.text: Level up knowing Ancient Power for Mamoswine.

evolutions.name: Gligar
evolutions.text: At night, level up holding (or use) a Razor Fang for Gliscor.

evolutions.name: Sneasel
evolutions.text: At night, level up holding (or use) a Razor Claw for Weavile. Hisuian Sneasel does the same by day for Sneasler.

evolutions.name: Ursaring
evolutions.text: Use a Peat Block at night for Ursaluna; at Mt. Moon at night it becomes Bloodmoon Ursaluna.

evolutions.name: Stantler
evolutions.text: Use Psyshield Bash 20 times, then level up, for Wyrdeer.

evolutions.name: Primeape
evolutions.text: Use Rage Fist 20 times, then level up, for Annihilape.

evolutions.name: Girafarig
evolutions.text: Level up knowing Twin Beam for Farigiraf.

evolutions.name: Dunsparce
evolutions.text: Level up knowing Hyper Drill for Dudunsparce.

evolutions.name: Happiny
evolutions.text: By day, level up holding (or use) an Oval Stone for Chansey; one is hidden in Rock Tunnel.
evolutions.source: pokehns-expansion Release-v2.0.6 source (species_info evolutions); pokehns-expansion Release-v2.0.6 source (map hidden items)

evolutions.name: Mantyke
evolutions.text: Level up with a Remoraid in the party for Mantine.

evolutions.name: Tyrogue
evolutions.text: At Lv 20: Hitmonlee if Attack is higher, Hitmonchan if Defense is, Hitmontop if equal.

evolutions.name: Kirlia
evolutions.text: Gardevoir at Lv 30; a male takes a Dawn Stone for Gallade.

evolutions.name: Snorunt
evolutions.text: Glalie at Lv 42; a female takes a Dawn Stone for Froslass.

evolutions.name: Togetic
evolutions.text: Shiny Stone for Togekiss.

evolutions.name: Roselia
evolutions.text: Shiny Stone for Roserade.

evolutions.name: Murkrow
evolutions.text: Dusk Stone for Honchkrow (one is hidden in Cerulean Cave).
evolutions.source: pokehns-expansion Release-v2.0.6 source (species_info evolutions); pokehns-expansion Release-v2.0.6 source (map hidden items)

evolutions.name: Misdreavus
evolutions.text: Dusk Stone for Mismagius.

evolutions.name: Bonsly
evolutions.text: Level up knowing Mimic for Sudowoodo.

evolutions.name: Mime Jr.
evolutions.text: Level up knowing Mimic for Mr. Mime.

evolutions.name: Nincada
evolutions.text: Ninjask at Lv 20; with a free party slot and a Poké Ball in the bag, Shedinja appears too.

evolutions.name: Qwilfish
evolutions.text: Hisuian Qwilfish (Route 49) levels up knowing Barb Barrage for Overqwil.

evolutions.name: Farfetch’d
evolutions.text: Galarian Farfetch'd (Bill's Teleporter) evolves into Sirfetch'd after landing 3 critical hits in one battle.

evolutions.name: Linoone
evolutions.text: Galarian Linoone (from a Galarian Zigzagoon, Teleporter) evolves at Lv 35 at night into Obstagoon.

notes.title: Heart & Soul 2.0
notes.text: A Gold/Silver/Crystal remake (and HeartGold/SoulSilver demake) on pokeemerald-expansion: Johto, then the Kanto post-game with all 16 badges. 2.0 was rebuilt from scratch: saves from 1.x don't load. Gen I-III species plus their later evolutions; abilities and items to Gen IX.
notes.source: Heart & Soul 2.0 documentation (pokemonhns-development.github.io); GitHub release notes

notes.title: Features
notes.text: Followers, overworld Pokémon, day and night, all 92 HGSS TMs, the Pokégear with radio and phone rematches, Kurt's Berry Balls, AutoRun and FastSurf, tutors that read the PC, an ability changer at the Saffron Dojo, Battle Frontier and Trainer Hill in Kanto.
notes.source: Heart & Soul 2.0 documentation (pokemonhns-development.github.io)

notes.title: Re-encounters
notes.text: Most static Pokémon come back if you run and re-enter; Celebi, Mew and Deoxys don't.
notes.source: Heart & Soul 2.0 documentation (pokemonhns-development.github.io)

notes.title: Entei and Raikou
notes.text: Both start roaming Johto at Lv 40 after the Burned Tower; Suicune is the one you chase to Route 25.
notes.source: Heart & Soul 2.0 documentation (pokemonhns-development.github.io)

notes.title: Trade evolutions
notes.text: A trade still works, but no trade is needed: Kadabra, Machoke, Graveler and Haunter evolve by level (42, 38, 38, 42), and the held-item ones evolve when you use the item on them like a stone (Metal Coat, King's Rock, Dragon Scale, Up-Grade, Dubious Disc, Protector, Electirizer, Magmarizer, Reaper Cloth, Deep Sea items, Prism Scale).
notes.source: pokehns-expansion Release-v2.0.6 source (species_info evolutions); H&S 2.0 documentation: FAQ

notes.title: Level caps
notes.text: With the level-cap setting on, the caps follow the gym leaders; after badge 8 they follow Johto Champion Lance's team, then Kanto Champion Lance's.
notes.source: H&S 2.0 documentation: FAQ

notes.title: Day and night
notes.text: Day is 6:00-18:59, night 19:00-5:59. There are no weekdays: daily events follow the clock, which the Pokémon Center can change (that may lock daily events for 24 hours).
notes.source: H&S 2.0 documentation: FAQ; H&S 2.0 documentation: Features

notes.title: Kanto Champion
notes.text: Beating the League again after the 16 badges makes you Kanto Champion. Legendaries and statics come back after each Kanto League win, and the roaming beasts are re-rolled (new shiny chance).
notes.source: pokehns-expansion Release-v2.0.6 source (Hall of Fame script); H&S documentation walkthrough (marked outdated); H&S 2.0 documentation: FAQ

notes.title: Bonus content: Sinjoh
notes.text: Optional after the Kanto post-game: the Azure Flute from Mt. Silver opens Snowswept Cavern, Routes 49-50, New Sinjoh and the Sinjoh Ruins, with Hisuian forms, noble Pokémon, the 17 plates, Steven, Arceus and six Regis at Lv 80.
notes.source: H&S 2.0 documentation: Features; H&S 2.0 documentation: Gifts & Statics; pokehns-expansion Release-v2.0.6 source

notes.title: Bonus content: the Isles
notes.text: With a Strange Souvenir from the Mt. Moon gift shop, the Route 13 boat goes to the Alola Isles: Alolan forms, static Alolan Pokémon and the Tapus at Lv 60, and Samson Oak.
notes.source: H&S 2.0 documentation: Features; H&S 2.0 documentation: Gifts & Statics; pokehns-expansion Release-v2.0.6 source

notes.title: Regional forms
notes.text: The main game has none; the bonus content brings them: Alolan on the Isles, Hisuian around Sinjoh, Galarian through Bill's Teleporter.
notes.source: H&S 2.0 documentation: FAQ; pokehns-expansion Release-v2.0.6 source

notes.title: Hoenn Pokémon
notes.text: Hoenn species appear as a 5% slot on each Kanto route (raised by the Hoenn Sound channel) and in the Kanto Safari Zone; Silph Co. gives the Hoenn starters.
notes.source: H&S 2.0 documentation: Features; H&S 2.0 documentation: Gifts & Statics

notes.title: Ho-Oh and Lugia
notes.text: Both can be caught. Each needs its wing, all eight Johto badges, Elm's Master Ball and the Kimono Girls beaten; the one Baoba's question picked is Lv 50, the other Lv 70.
notes.source: H&S 2.0 documentation: FAQ; H&S 2.0 documentation: Gifts & Statics; H&S documentation walkthrough (marked outdated)

notes.title: Latias and Latios
notes.text: One waits on Southern Island at Lv 50, the other roams Kanto at Lv 60; running resets them.
notes.source: H&S 2.0 documentation: Gifts & Statics; H&S 2.0 documentation: Features

notes.title: Shiny roamers
notes.text: Entei's and Raikou's shininess and IVs are fixed when they are released; save before the Burned Tower to retry, or win the Kanto League to re-roll them.
notes.source: H&S 2.0 documentation: FAQ

notes.title: Hoenn legendaries
notes.text: With 16 badges: Kyogre in a cave off Route 19, Groudon in a hidden Seafoam cave, Rayquaza in the Embedded Tower (Route 47), all Lv 70; Jirachi, Mew, Deoxys and the Latis by ticket or event.
notes.source: H&S 2.0 documentation: Gifts & Statics; H&S documentation walkthrough (marked outdated)

notes.title: Arceus and the Regis
notes.text: In the Sinjoh Ruins: Arceus and Regirock, Regice, Registeel, Regigigas, Regieleki, Regidrago, all Lv 80.
notes.source: H&S 2.0 documentation: Gifts & Statics

notes.title: In-game trades
notes.text: Ten trades plus Jessica's Tauros: Onix (Violet), Machop (Goldenrod), Steelix (Jasmine), Voltorb (Olivine), Mr. Mime (Blackthorn), Haunter and Bonsly (Pewter), Magneton (Power Plant), Beldum (Safari Zone), Meowth (Battle Frontier). Trades and tutors can use Pokémon in the PC.
notes.source: H&S 2.0 documentation: Gifts & Statics; H&S 2.0 documentation: Features

notes.title: Gift Pokémon
notes.text: Eevee (Bill), Shuckle, Spearow and Tentacool loans, Tyrogue (Mt. Mortar), Dratini (Dragon's Den), fossils at the Ruins of Alph lab, the Hoenn starters and Paldean Wooper; the Game Corner sells Abra, Clefairy, Munchlax, Dratini and Porygon.
notes.source: H&S 2.0 documentation: Gifts & Statics

notes.title: Battle Frontier
notes.text: Trainer Hill (via Route 40) opens after the Johto League; the modern-Emerald Battle Frontier and Battle Tents are reached in Kanto. "Level 50" sets any Pokémon to 50; "Open Level" uses current levels.
notes.source: H&S documentation walkthrough (marked outdated); H&S 2.0 documentation: Features
